title: Health claim lifecycle
objective: New claims processors follow one claim from intake to payment and see the rules that decide whether it pends, is denied, is appealed or gets paid.

recommended.why: A clickable flow diagram shows every possible route at once, lights up the one this claim takes, and lets learners click any step for its rule.

alternative.why: A clickable diagram versus a hand-drawn swimlane: convenience versus flexibility.

assumptions: Illustrative, generic process and wording; not any specific health plan's rules, systems or forms
The member has active coverage on the date of service
A missing prior authorization always leads to a denial; an appeal is only possible after a denial
A pended claim always gets its records back and resumes; time limits and partial payments are not modelled
Amounts are illustrative: $1,240 billed, $860 allowed, $160 member cost share, $700 paid by the plan
Event times are playback seconds for the explainer, not real processing days
checkDescription: Every event is at a real station and is a legal next step in time order, a denial happens exactly when prior auth is missing, an appeal only follows a denial, and the claim is paid only if eligible, authorized when required, and never denied or won on appeal.

learnerPrompts.predict: Set prior authorization to Missing. Before you press play: which steps will the claim visit, and will the member's EOB show any payment?
learnerPrompts.explain: Turn on missing information. Why does the claim go back to adjudication instead of being denied, and what does that mean for the provider?
